changes: Collect the entire already-permitted src/peft/tuners/oft package, retaining __init__.py and any submitted sibling helpers. Canonical finalization updates Harbor artifacts and deletes the full baseline package before import.
Add an equivalent that moves OFTRotationModule byte-for-byte into rotation.py and imports it from layer.py; methods, registration paths and arithmetic remain unchanged.
Compact four duplicate control rationales to stay within the bounded reviewer input. All existing test code, thresholds, public requirements, control scripts and Gold remain unchanged.
limitations: No target/Torch/probe/control/Gold execution, paid calls or launch.
Fresh remote validation remains necessary; static transfer checks do not claim execution evidence.

blockers: Artifact collection can silently drop a permitted submission layout. instruction.md says "Submit your changes under `src/peft/tuners/oft/` (at least `config.py`, `layer.py`, and ... `model.py`)", i.e. extra helper modules in that package are allowed, but task.toml lists only those three files as [[artifacts]] and tests/Dockerfile deletes exactly those three from the image. A correct solution that factors, e.g., the rotation module into `src/peft/tuners/oft/rotation.py` imported by layer.py would have that file absent in the verifier image; every probe would raise ImportError and score 0 despite satisfying the public contract.
repairs: Close the artifact/instruction gap: either add an [[artifacts]] entry for the whole `/workspace/src/peft/tuners/oft/` directory (runner.py already rglobs directory sources) and delete the whole package dir in tests/Dockerfile before copying, or state explicitly in instruction.md that only config.py, layer.py and model.py are graded and no new modules may be added.
evidence: task.toml artifacts list only .../oft/config.py, layer.py, model.py; tests/Dockerfile `RUN rm -rf /workspace/src/peft/tuners/oft/{config,layer,model}.py` — any additional submitted module in that package is never transferred.

tests/test_contract.py `_reference_forward`/`_exact_cayley`/`_neumann_cayley` are independent NumPy oracles; forward tests compare probe output to them at rtol/atol 1e-4 for exact, shared, 2/3/18-term Neumann, block_size 3 and 4 (row-major triu ordering), so wrong sign, wrong series truncation, transposed R or ignored `use_cayley_neumann` are all detected.

test_input_rotation_calls_unchanged_frozen_base uses TorchDispatchMode to capture mm/addmm/linear operands, requires a projection whose weight equals unchanged W.T and whose left rows are exactly the rotated inputs (both orientations permitted) — rejects the rotate_weight mutation while admitting the F.linear and (W @ rows.T).T equivalents.

test_oft_r_weight_is_trainable_with_nonzero_gradient checks grad against central finite differences of the independent reference (rtol 2e-3), for exact/Neumann, shared and zero-init cases, and asserts max|expected|>1e-6, so detach/no_grad and constant-rotation implementations fail; `trainable_names == ["base_model.model.proj.oft_R.default.weight"]` keeps base weight/bias frozen and forbids a surviving scale parameter (frozen auxiliary params remain permitted).

_assert_merge_cycles checks forward==merged_out==post-unmerge==second cycle plus restored weight/bias == fixed W/b, and merged_weight == (Rfull @ W.T).T; test_merge_unmerge_block_share_and_neumann includes num_terms=2 where R is visibly non-orthogonal, so transpose-as-inverse unmerge is caught (consistent with instruction.md item 4 'unmerging exactly restores').

test_three_dimensional_inputs_rotate_only_last_dimension asserts shape (2,3,4) and reassigns `updated_block_params` after all merge observations, giving a genuine post-update state check that defeats rotation caching and 2D-only rotation.

solution/patch.diff Linear.__init__ defaults `use_cayley_neumann: bool = False` while OFTConfig defaults True; model.py always forwards the config value, so peft-path behavior matches the spec (CONFIG_PROBE checks the config defaults 0/32/True/5).
optional_improvements: Runtime risk: the suite spawns ~27 separate run_probe subprocesses (3+2 parametrizations, 4 each in merge/grad/input-rotation, 2 rank-only), each re-importing torch+peft, against a 240 s pytest timeout in runner.py on 2 CPUs. Consider batching more cases with _run_many/_batch_worker to avoid flaky timeouts; actual wall time is unmeasured here.
Align Linear.__init__'s `use_cayley_neumann=False` default with the config default True in GOLD to avoid confusing direct-construction semantics (untested either way).

The payload keys `check_base_no_op`/`check_merge_no_op` are set by _small_case but never read in BUILD_MODEL_AND_RUN; remove them or implement the intended observation to avoid a false sense of coverage.
Zero-init no-op is only exercised with use_cayley_neumann=False; adding the Neumann/shared variants to test_default_init_is_identity_no_op would broaden the identity check cheaply.

before_contract.title: OFT adapter: compact skew-symmetric parametrization with exact/Cayley-Neumann rotation
before_contract.rationale: The PEFT OFT tuner was reworked to store only the free parameters of each block's skew-symmetric generator, drop the separate per-channel scale, apply the resulting orthogonal rotation directly to the layer input instead of rebuilding a rotated weight matrix every forward pass, and support both the exact Cayley transform and a cheaper truncated Cayley-Neumann series approximation. This task isolates that behavior for torch.nn.Linear-based OFT adapters.

requirements.behavior: The OFT adapter for a Linear layer stores its trainable parameters as oft_R[<adapter>].weight of shape (num_blocks, block_size*(block_size-1)//2), with num_blocks==1 when block_share=True. named_parameters() on a get_peft_model-wrapped model expose the parameter as '...oft_R.default.weight' and never 'oft_r'/'oft_s'. The vec->skew mapping follows the row-major strict-upper-triangle convention. Only the compact weight is trainable; additional frozen auxiliary parameters are permitted.

OFTConfig exposes use_cayley_neumann (default True) and num_cayley_neumann_terms (default 5); r defaults to 0 and oft_block_size defaults to 32; specifying both r!=0 and oft_block_size!=0 (or neither) raises ValueError.

forward() rotates the input features block-by-block with the exact Cayley rotation R=(I+S)^-1(I-S) of each block's skew-symmetric generator (no per-channel scale) and passes the result through the frozen base layer; the output matches a NumPy reference computed from the same generator values, for both block_share=False and block_share=True, and use_cayley_neumann=False always uses the exact transform regardless of num_cayley_neumann_terms. Direct functional linear projection of rotated input by unchanged frozen base parameters is also valid; module invocation is not required. Preserve all leading input axes and rotate only the final feature axis for 3D inputs, in exact/Neumann and shared/unshared modes. A subsequent forward reflects a newly assigned compact weight in all four modes. Either multiplication orientation of unchanged W and rotated input is valid.
A freshly initialized adapter (default init_weights=True) has oft_R["default"].weight all zeros, so S=0, R=I, and forward/merge exactly reproduce the unwrapped base_layer's output.

With use_cayley_neumann=True, num_cayley_neumann_terms=1 gives R=I (forward equals the unrotated base-layer output) and num_cayley_neumann_terms=2/3 give the exact truncated-series value I-2S(+2S^2); increasing num_cayley_neumann_terms further makes the forward output converge to the exact-Cayley output for small-norm generators.

merge() folds the block rotation into base_layer.weight so that the merged base layer alone reproduces the pre-merge adapted forward output; unmerge() exactly restores the original base_layer weight and bias; this holds for block_share=True and for use_cayley_neumann=True as well as the default exact/non-shared path. Adapted forwarding remains correct after unmerge and after a second complete merge/unmerge cycle.

Exact and default Neumann transforms preserve mathematically correct finite gradients on the compact trainable tensor, including shared blocks and zero initialization; base weight and bias stay frozen.

equivalents.name: explicit_loop_block_diagonal
equivalents.rationale: Build the identical block-diagonal rotation by explicit block placement instead of torch.block_diag.
equivalents.script:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
path = 'src/peft/tuners/oft/layer.py'
s = open(path).read()
old = '''        if self.block_share:
            orth_rotate = orth_rotate.repeat(rank, 1, 1)

        x_rotated = torch.einsum("...rk,rkc->...rc", x_reshaped, orth_rotate)
        x_rotated = x_rotated.reshape(*x.shape)'''
new = '''        if self.block_share:
            orth_rotate = orth_rotate.repeat(rank, 1, 1)

        # Equivalent to the einsum contraction, computed one block at a time.
        rotated_blocks = [
            torch.matmul(x_reshaped[..., i, :], orth_rotate[i]) for i in range(orth_rotate.shape[0])
        ]
        x_rotated = torch.stack(rotated_blocks, dim=-2)
        x_rotated = x_rotated.reshape(*x.shape)'''
assert old in s, 'anchor not found'
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
open(path, 'w').write(s)

positive_control.name: rotation_in_sibling_module
positive_control.rationale: Move the unchanged rotation class into rotation.py; relative import preserves behavior and parameter paths. The permitted package helper must reach the verifier.
positive_control.script:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
import ast
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('src/peft/tuners/oft/layer.py')
s = p.read_text()
nodes = [n for n in ast.parse(s).body if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == 'OFTRotationModule']
assert len(nodes) == 1
n = nodes[0]
lines = s.splitlines(keepends=True)
block = ''.join(lines[n.lineno - 1:n.end_lineno])
helper = p.with_name('rotation.py')
assert not helper.exists()
helper.write_text('from __future__ import annotations\nimport torch\nimport torch.nn as nn\n\n' + block)
p.write_text(''.join(lines[:n.lineno - 1]) + 'from .rotation import OFTRotationModule\n' + ''.join(lines[n.end_lineno:]))
PY
